scope: M1 copy/fill trust boundary; later experiments are recorded separately below

logical.claim: dst and src are nonzero, including n=0
dst+n and src+n do not exceed 2^64
input and output regions are disjoint
aligned actual code bytes are loaded, output does not overlap code
logical.provider: caller/model precondition; object and linked-byte checks

logical.claim: the word path has both addresses aligned to 8 and a full remaining word
logical.provider: proved guard and loop invariant; not added to public precondition

logical.claim: child code placement, register values, frame and bounded memory window hold at each composition
each valid call reaches its return address in finitely many model steps
logical.provider: HOL while invariants and finite natural-number bound

external.claim: data denotes mapped ordinary RAM of the required lifetime and permissions; writes are exclusive
external.status: trusted external correspondence, not a predicate proving OS validity

external.claim: code is mapped executable and remains stable during execution
pinned s2n-bignum ARM semantics corresponds to the executing CPU for the used forms
external.status: assumed physical correspondence; E6a provides finite differential evidence, not full ISA/CPU equivalence

external.claim: HOL Light kernel, OCaml implementation, runtime and their build execute soundly

external.claim: the independently written contracts express the intended copy/fill requirements
external.provider: specification review and independent native references

external.claim: object import, Python Mach-O extraction and LLVM position listings identify the bytes that the OS executes
external.provider: unverified tools and loader; exact-byte comparisons
external.status: checked evidence plus remaining trust; not a verified linker

external.claim: C harness, benchmark compiler, clock, counters and report aggregation behave as intended
external.status: finite supplemental evidence; not HOL proofs

external.claim: the external caller provides an ABI-valid return target and invocation context

external.status: external correspondence; logical theorems quantify the model returnaddress without proving loader/ABI validity
